text:
anya: heads up — bringing up Mistral4 quant profiles (AWQ + GPTQ). On CUDA19 + Triton we see a repeating tiling/misalignment artifact at generation time, sometimes falls back to vLLM and then outputs shift.
chetan: can you paste the exact cmd/config you used? and a short sample of the failing log
anya: repro cmd:\n```
run_bench --model mistral4 --quant awq --backend trtllm --cuda 19 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --config configs/mistral4-awq.json
```
log snippet:\n```
[2026-03-19T12:08:22Z] kernel: tiled_len != expected_len (4096 != 4092) in attention_kern.cu:254
[2026-03-19T12:08:22Z] runtime: kernel launch succeeded but result checksum mismatch, falling back to runtime vLLM path
```
sam: hmm tiling mismatch + checksum mismatch usually points at ABI/kernel registration or an optimization path that assumes different alignment. which triton container tag? and what trtllm plugin version?
anya: triton: 23.09.0-custom, trtllm-plugin: 1.4.2, driver: 535.54, libcudnn 9.2. saw the checksum in ~30% of runs
maria: driver 535.x had a regression for certain attention fusions on Ampere->Hopper variant in CUDA19 land. Noticed similar with AWQ's fused kernels — they assume 64-byte alignment for tiled KV buffers. If runtime or kernel build uses a different pack stride it corrupts tails.
chetan: can you try forcing the fallback off so we see the raw failure? set env TRITON_DISABLE_FALLBACK=1 and run minimal gen (seq512) to reproduce quickly
anya: tried that — explicit crash: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS on attention_kern.cu:248. stacktrace points to trtllm fused attention.
sam: two quick mitigation options: 1) disable tiling/fusion in trtllm for AWQ (env like TRTLLM_DISABLE_TILING=1) 2) route AWQ workloads on this model to vLLM runtime for now (slower but numerically stable)
maria: also try setting TRITON_CUDA_GRAPH=0 — there were reports interaction between CUDA graphs and fused kernels in this driver build.
anya: tested both: export TRTLLM_DISABLE_TILING=1 -> generation succeeds with correct checksums and eval accuracy back to baseline, throughput drops ~18%. export TRITON_CUDA_GRAPH=0 -> small improvement but still unstable unless tiling disabled.
chetan: what about GPTQ path? is it affected the same way?
anya: GPTQ builds use a different kernel set — when I switched quant to GPTQ and re-ran same triton container, no tiling mismatch; accuracy delta: AWQ (original, with tiling) -> eval BLEU -0.9, AWQ (tiling disabled) -> BLEU -0.1 relative to fp16, GPTQ -> BLEU -0.05. So AWQ+tiling had correctness noise.
sam: OK actionable plan: add a canary routing rule in the serving config: for model=mistral4 + quant=awq + driver_version >=535 and <=537 -> route to vLLM fallback or set TRTLLM_DISABLE_TILING env for dedicated pools. Also log "quant_tiling_issue" metric and trigger alert if checksum mismatches > 1%.
maria: I'll open a bug with trtllm plugin and attach the failing kernel checksum/tail data. include the exact kernel build id and a small repro binary. also escalate to infra to test on driver 536.86 and 538.x
infra-bot: canary rule created: mistral4-awq-tiling-fallback, scope=staging, rollout=5% :link:
anya: thanks — can we add eval gating so that new quant builds run the tiny eval suite (1k examples) and fail rollout if checksum mismatches or BLEU delta <-0.5?
sam: yes, add eval-gate: {threshold: -0.5, metric: bleu, fallback_on_fail: true} and add telemetry tag `quant_onboard:mistral4:awq:tiling` to all requests during rollout
anya: will run the 1k eval on the latest AWQ candidate with TRTLLM_DISABLE_TILING=1 and without it, and push results to the bench dashboard
maria: also note: long-term we should get a kernel fix to enable tiling safely; disabling tiling loses perf. I'll coordinate with plugin maintainers.
anya: uploading quick bench report now — link: https://bench.redwood.internal/runs/2050012345 (contains per-model BLEU/latency/cpu/gpu mem)
sam: nice, thanks. if infra can validate on driver 538 tomorrow we can remove the canary and re-enable tiling if kernel fix lands.
chetan: logging: created issue ML-quant-1123 "mistral4 awq trtllm tiling checksum" and attached logs
anya: perfect — landing smoke tests and gating today. :thumbsup:
